messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Interesting Bayesian Deep Learning Blog Post

Since they're using the same algorithm as in Stan, it should
work in Stan if someone wants to code it up. I coded some
simple three-level networks (one hidden level), but the efficiency
from MCMC isn't there and I don't really know how to do all
the semi-supervision tricks they use to train deeper networks.

- Bob

> On Sep 12, 2016, at 3:44 PM, John Hall <john.mic...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I noticed it was the same. It helps being able to leverage already existing Python libraries (that I believe can also use GPUs for the calculations). Maybe there's a C++ neural net library that could be called from user-defined functions in Stan? Probably would need some glue to get it working.

I believe PyMC3 calls Theano for derivatives, so any GPU tie-ins
would probably have to come through that.

What we need for Stan is C++ functions with derivatives. And
it needs to build everywhere if we're going to release it as
part of Stan. For details on what is required to add a function
to Stan:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Contributing-New-Functions-to-Stan

- Bob
